deviations.what: t5 also adds a minimal 'Log out' button (form POST /logout) to the approved user's header in templates/index.html.j2
deviations.reason: the plan requires POST /logout but names no way to reach it from the UI; without a button logout is unusable

deviations.what: t6 adds config key auth.app_signin.base_url (falls back to media.public_base_url; set-password routes disabled with a logged error if neither is set) for building set-password links
deviations.reason: link host must come from trusted config, never the request Host header (reset-link host injection); the plan named no base-URL source

deviations.what: t6 adds RedactTokenFilter on the aiohttp.access, irc_lens.web.auth/csrf/routes loggers, rewriting /password/<token> to /password/[redacted]
deviations.reason: the token-logging test showed aiohttp's access log and the auth middleware wrote the full set-password token into the journal; c33 forbids codes in logs

deviations.what: t9 checks the guest limit before verifying the code, so a guest refused as busy keeps an unused code (the brief accepted a consumed one); a verified slot is reserved for 120 s until the browser opens it
deviations.reason: kinder to the refused guest and spends no extra email; reservation closes the check-then-open race

deviations.what: r6 decided by owner: replace the per-email code-entry limit (5/15min) and the 5-codes-per-15-min cap with trusted browsers (no limit) plus an escalating per-email budget for untrusted browsers (3/15min, then 2/30min), silent when blocked
deviations.reason: owner decision on risk r6: the old per-email limit let anyone who knows an approved email block its sign-in

deviations.what: owner adds a new-browser sign-in notice email (c40) to the app sign-in PR, after the review fixes
deviations.reason: owner request during review of #68: users should learn of sign-ins from browsers they have not trusted

deviations.what: code entries no longer count toward the per-IP limit or the per-email untrusted budget (amends c38/h27: those count password submissions only); no limit on code entries
deviations.reason: live go-live: an owner's second browser on the same IP had its correct code silently refused, because the first sign-in's code entry used an IP slot; code guessing is infeasible, so counting codes only locked out the real user
